items.name: CO₂ jet
items.product: UPlight UP-Q108S "CO2 gas column gun" — UPlight's own store and site list no UP-Q108S; not one of their traceable products. Described here as the general class of DMX CO2 jet, modelled on the MagicFX CO2jet II.
items.what: A single vertical blast of white gas straight up out of a nozzle. Liquid CO2 flashes to gas and dry-ice snow the instant it leaves the valve, so the jet looks like a thick white column of smoke — but it is a gas release, not a fog machine. It fires with a loud, sharp hiss and is genuinely cold at the nozzle. Each shot lasts a few seconds and the column reaches roughly 8 m.
items.inShow: Fired on a single hit or drop for one loud vertical burst, then off — not run continuously. Needs a fresh, correctly plumbed liquid-CO2 bottle for every handful of shots, and clear air space directly above the nozzle.

needs.text: liquid CO2 in a cylinder with an internal dip tube (siphon tube) — a standard gas cylinder without a dip tube will not feed liquid to the jet.

CO2 is about 1.5x denser than air and settles at floor level; in an enclosed or low-ceilinged room repeated firing can build up an asphyxiation hazard that is not obvious to the people breathing it. Ventilate continuously or use a CO2/oxygen monitor for any sustained indoor use, and never fire into a confined space.
the CO2 cylinder must be secured upright (strapped or caged) and connected with a rated high-pressure CO2 hose and bottle-to-hose connector — never a loose or unsecured bottle.
standard mains (220-240 Vac); the jet's own power draw is small (20 W), the cold gas comes from the bottle's pressure, not from the machine.

specs.label: plume height
specs.value: approx. 8 m, depends on humidity (equivalent product)

specs.label: CO2 consumption
specs.value: approx. 0.5 kg per second of firing (equivalent product)

alternatives.why: the named product this class is modelled on here; full manual and specs published.
US supplier with a published range from handheld to mounted high-output jets and its own safety literature.
a CO2-free alternative — an LED-lit pyro-look fog burst with no gas cylinder, no asphyxiation risk and no bottle logistics; the trade-off is it is fog, not a real gas column.

items.name: cold-spark machine
items.product: UPlight UP-YH600F "Cold-spark firework machine" — UPlight's own store and site list no UP-YH600F; not one of their traceable products. Described here as the general class of DMX cold-spark machine, modelled on the Showven Sparkular.
items.what: A box that heats a metal granule powder and blows it upward as a controlled fountain of bright white sparks — it looks like an indoor firework but the sparks are far cooler by the time they leave the nozzle and are not a flame or combustion effect. It is waterproof-rated. Adjustable spark height is roughly 1.5-5 m, and it is genuinely quieter than a real firework.
items.inShow: Fired on a cue for a bright, camera-ready burst timed to music or a lighting cue; height and duration are set per cue over DMX.

needs.text: spark granules — a titanium/magnesium/zirconium metal powder, sold and refilled by weight; not reusable.

even though it needs no fireworks/explosives licence in most jurisdictions, it is still hot particulate ejected under pressure: run a venue fire-safety check before use, and keep audience and any flammable material at least 1.5-2 m from the machine and at least 1 m clear above the set maximum spark height.
an operator who sets spark height/duration and checks the machine's own tilt and overheat interlocks before firing.

specs.label: clearance
specs.value: 1.5-2 m to audience/flammables, 1 m above max spark height

alternatives.why: the original cold-spark machine and the product this class is modelled on; the most widely rented unit in this class.
built-in tilt/overheat/blocked-output safety sensors and an FX warning LED; published manual with clearance distances.
US supplier's own cold-spark line, sold alongside the Sparkular for the same rental market.

items.name: smoke machine
items.product: UPlight UP-YZ31P "Smoke machine (multi-angle)" — UPlight's own store and site list no UP-YZ31P; not one of their traceable products. Described here as the general class of waterproof fog machine, modelled on the Antari Z-1500 III.
items.what: Fog fluid is heated to vapour inside the box and pushed out through an aimable nozzle as a dense, clearly visible white cloud — this is theatrical "smoke" in the technical sense: thicker and more opaque than haze, made to fill a space or be lit as its own visible shape, not just to reveal beams. UPlight's "multi-angle" nozzle can be aimed; the unit is rated waterproof for outdoor use.
items.inShow: Laid down to build a heavy layer of atmosphere, hide a scene change, or catch a strong light for a visible beam or silhouette; needs several minutes' warm-up and steady fluid feed to sustain output.

needs.text: visible smoke will trigger a ceiling-mounted photoelectric smoke detector; any use in a monitored venue needs the fire alarm system's detectors isolated in advance with the venue's fire marshal or safety officer, a fire watch kept on the isolated zone, and the detectors restored immediately after.

specs.value: approx. 150 ml/min at full output (equivalent product)

1300 W, fine-step 0-99% output control and a 5-pin DMX interface, widely used in theatre and touring rigs.

items.name: low-fog machine
items.product: UPlight UP-SW3000B "Low-fog machine 3000W" (double-head ground fog) — UPlight's own store and site list no UP-SW3000B; not one of their traceable products. Described here as the general class of double-output 3000 W low-lying (ground) fog machine.
items.what: A fog machine built to lay fog on the floor rather than fill the room: the fog fluid is heated, then cooled again — either by mixing with dry ice or, in the water-based design used here as the reference, by passing through a chilled, ultrasonic-atomiser chamber — so the fog comes out heavier than the surrounding air and hugs the ground instead of rising. This gives the classic knee-high "ground mist" look without needing dry ice on site.
items.inShow: Run for a short period before or at the start of a scene to build a still, low layer that performers' legs move through; a 3000 W double-output unit can fill roughly 70 m² in under two minutes but needs the room's air kept still to stay low.

needs.text: water-based low-lying fog fluid specifically (ordinary fog fluid will rise rather than stay grounded), plus distilled water for the cooling/atomiser chamber — tap-water minerals damage the ultrasonic atomisers.
ground fog usually sits below ceiling-mounted smoke detectors but this must be tested in the venue beforehand, the same as any fog use.

specs.label: coverage
specs.value: approx. 70 m² in about 100 seconds (equivalent product)

specs.label: control
specs.value: DMX, 2 channels: channel 1 output volume, channel 2 timing/interval (equivalent product)

alternatives.why: the product this class is modelled on; dry-ice-free double-output design with published specs.
the traditional dry-ice route to the same look — a lift mechanism dips dry ice into hot water; a real, well-stocked alternative if dry ice is available on site.

items.name: butterfly effect light
items.product: UPlight UP-HD210 "3-in-1 butterfly effect" (multi-effect) — UPlight's own store and site list no UP-HD210; not one of their traceable products. Described here as the general class of compact 3-in-1 party-light fixture, using the AVSL "Butterfly Effect 3-in-1" as a named comparable product.
items.what: A single small fixture that combines three separate effects in one box: rotating multi-beam LED patterns (the "butterfly" — the same idea as a derby light), a low-power red/green laser that throws a star-field of fine beam lines, and a set of coloured LED PARs / a strobe. It is a one-box party-light solution rather than a precision fixture — sold to cover a small stage or dance floor with moving colour and laser texture from a single unit.
items.inShow: Run as a continuous automatic, sound-activated, or DMX-controlled wash of moving colour and fine laser lines over a crowd or small stage — a texture-filler rather than a fixture aimed at anything specific.

needs.text: the comparable product's laser is class 3B (per IEC 60825-1's hazard classes): direct or specular viewing of the beam can injure the eye. It needs the same basic laser precautions as any laser fixture in the rig — no aiming into the audience at eye level, and whoever runs the show should know where its beams sweep.

items.name: hazer
items.product: Not on the rental house's list — the rig needs haze to make its beams visible. Reference product: MDG ATMe haze generator.
items.what: Haze is a very fine, even mist — droplets under a micron across, far smaller than fog or smoke — spread through the air so it barely reads as a cloud but makes every beam of light passing through it look like a solid shaft. It is the standard way moving-light and laser beams are made visible in a room without laying down a visible cloud the way a fog or smoke machine does; fog/smoke is thicker, denser, and meant to be seen as its own shape, while haze is meant to stay unnoticed except where a beam cuts through it.
items.inShow: Run continuously at a low, steady level through a scene — unlike fog, which is used in short bursts — so every beam, gobo edge and laser line reads clearly to the eye and on camera. Too much haze and the room itself starts to look milky.

needs.text: haze fluid — a highly refined white mineral oil for the MDG ATMe's own 'Neutral' fluid.
a CO2 cylinder as the carrier gas (the MDG ATMe design draws on CO2, not just mains air, to atomise the fluid): about 0.18-0.36 kg/hour depending on output pressure.

haze is a far lower particle dose than fog, but the same basic care applies in a small closed room: don't run it without some air movement, and check with the venue if it shares an HVAC zone with smoke detectors.
